coordinates.locator: CERN Courier, "Baksan scales new neutrino heights" (19 May 2017): SAGE lies 3.5 km from the tunnel entrance; OpenStreetMap node 4244310615 (Main adit entrance, 43.2756023 N 42.6921682 E)
coordinates.note: Campus-grade: the point is the OpenStreetMap Main adit entrance of the Baksan Neutrino Observatory, not the laboratory. CERN Courier and the SAGE 1999 results paper put the SAGE laboratory 3.5 km from the entrance of a horizontal adit; no source read gives the tunnel's bearing or says which of the observatory's parallel adits it is, so the laboratory lies within about 3.5 km (precision stated 3500 m) of this point. It is not a surveyed underground position (rank-11 OpenStreetMap source, A17), and no published coordinate of the laboratory itself was found. The previous point, about 150 m to the west, was a coarse point (precision 3000 m) for the same area.
coordinates.quote: SAGE, which has been in operation since 1986 and is led by Vladimir Gavrin, is located 3.5 km from the tunnel entrance

depth.display: ~2100 m of rock above the laboratory
depth.locator: Slide 'Baksan Valley and Mt. Andyrchi' (page 7 of the PDF)
depth.note: Rock thickness above the SAGE (GGNT) laboratory per the Baksan Neutrino Observatory's 2016 presentation; the SAGE 1999 paper gives the overburden as 4700 m.w.e. (see depth_mwe).
depth.quote: GGNT - 3,5 km from the entrance 2100 m thickness of the rock above laboratory (4700 m.w.e.)

depth_mwe.note: Overhead shielding of the SAGE gallium laboratory, 3.5 km from the entrance of the horizontal adit into Mount Andyrchi (SAGE 1999 results paper).
depth_mwe.quote: has an overhead shielding of 4700 meters of water equivalent

muon_flux.note: Muon flux at the SAGE gallium experiment in its deep hall; the paper states no energy threshold or reference surface. Pandola 2011, Table 1, lists 3.03 × 10^-5 m^-2 s^-1 for the SAGE hall, citing an INR report of 1991 (V. N. Gavrin et al.), and gives 4800 m w.e. as the hall's vertical depth against the 4700 m.w.e. of the SAGE paper.
muon_flux.quote: The rock overburden is equivalent to 4700 m of water and the measured muon flux at the location of the experiment is (3.03±0.10)×10−9 /(cm2 s).

summary.plain: A chamber under more than two kilometres of rock in a mountain in the Russian Caucasus, holding tonnes of liquid gallium metal to catch solar neutrinos.
summary.technical: Underground laboratory of the Baksan Neutrino Observatory, under about 2100 m of rock (4700 m.w.e.) in the Caucasus Mountains, Kabardino-Balkaria, Russia, housing the SAGE gallium detector.
